title: Upstream and downstream policy push: Europe Regional Spotlight
gist: Teaser of a Benchmark Europe regional spotlight: Europe has a small upstream and downstream footprint in the battery supply chain versus China and the US, with no major battery mineral mined or processed primarily on the continent. The EU's Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) policy package aims to build manufacturing presence to serve EV and BESS demand expected to grow significantly through 2040; full article is behind registration.

insights.claim: Europe's upstream and downstream footprint in the global battery supply chain is small compared with China and the US.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: European battery supply chain remains import-dependent, exposing EU automakers and storage developers to Chinese and US supply.
insights.quote: Compared with China and the US, Europe’s upstream and downstream footprint in the global battery supply chain footprint is small.
insights.locator: Compared with China and the US

insights.claim: No major critical mineral used in batteries is mined or processed primarily in Europe, and cathode, anode and cell production are not centred on the continent either.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Every stage from mining to cells is a potential policy-driven investment opportunity or vulnerability for Europe.
insights.quote: No major critical mineral used in the sector is mined or processed primarily on the continent
insights.locator: Compared with China and the US

insights.claim: The EU's Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) is a policy package intended to boost Europe's manufacturing presence across the battery industry.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: IAA could channel subsidies/local-content rules toward European battery materials and cell makers.
insights.quote: a package of policies under the EU’s Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA) is looking to boost its manufacturing presence in the industry

insights.claim: Building domestic battery manufacturing is framed as necessary if Europe is to meet more of its own EV and battery energy storage demand, both of which are expected to grow significantly through 2040.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Long-dated EV and BESS demand growth underpins the case for European battery capacity build-out.
